subject.title: fix(secrets): keep standalone-tool provider credentials active when a different provider is selected

question: Is a non-empty generic plugin `contracts.tools` declaration the intended permanent authorization for activating that plugin's web-provider credential when it is not the selected generic web search or fetch provider?
rationale: This determines the supported secret-activation contract and whether the new runtime snapshot intentionally includes credentials for all tool-bearing provider plugins or only providers explicitly tied to standalone web tools.

options.title: Require explicit web-tool eligibility
options.body: Narrow the resolver to a provider/manifest signal that explicitly proves the credential is shared by standalone web tools, and add regression coverage for unrelated tool contracts.

options.title: Accept generic tool contracts
options.body: Document that every effectively enabled plugin with `contracts.tools` may activate its web-provider credential and accept the expanded startup/reload failure boundary.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Hold this PR if the plugin manifest needs a new or clarified contract before secret eligibility can be safely encoded.

recommendation.title: Require explicit web-tool eligibility
recommendation.body: Narrow the resolver to a provider/manifest signal that explicitly proves the credential is shared by standalone web tools, and add regression coverage for unrelated tool contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author can explain the intended contract and incorporate the chosen owner direction; a current-main feature owner was not independently identifiable from the available read-only evidence.
